name: Ginza Sushi
blocked: Menufy/HungerRush storefront on the restaurant's own domain (ginzasushirb.com, location_menufy_id 48900, address 16715 Bernardo Center Dr, San Diego matches batch). Read the full priced catalog: 239 items across 15 categories (Beverage, Appetizer, Salad, Sushi Sashimi Box, Maki Sushi, Chef Special Sushi, Protein Roll, Nigiri & Sashimi, Korean Cuisine, Noodle & Fried Rice, Bowls, Soft Tofu Soup, Bibimbap, Catering, Lunch Special) -- but ran the markup test and 225/239 prices (94%) divide cleanly by 1.04 onto round dollar figures (e.g. $5.20->$5.00, $18.72->$18.00, $114.40->$110.00). That is a ~4% online-ordering surcharge baked into the storefront, same pattern flagged in the playbook for other Clover/Menufy platforms carrying a POS service fee. These are not the prices on the wall. Holding as blocked pending an unmarked-up source (dine-in photo/PDF or another channel) rather than filing surcharge prices.
notes: Full menu was reachable and complete in shape (sushi, sashimi, rolls, Korean bowls, noodles, catering, lunch specials) -- the only problem is the ~4% markup, not missing coverage.

name: We Olive & Wine Bar
notes: weolive.com now redirects to shop.weolive.com and the La Jolla location page (weolive.com/la-jolla/) 404s -- the site no longer publishes a menu at all. Found the old page via the Wayback Machine (snapshot dated 2025-01-17), which linked four PDFs hosted on the same now-dead page: 'Food Menu' (filename dated Spring 2024), 'Beer Menu' (link itself is malformed/broken, 404 even via Wayback), 'White Wines' and 'Red Wines' (both dated (c) 2023 in their own header text). Pulled the archived PDFs through web.archive.org and read them with pdftotext -raw (the -layout mode scrambles this two-column price/description layout into wrong name-price pairs, exactly the failure mode the playbook warns about for wine lists -- raw reading order pairs each item with its price correctly). Filed ONLY the food menu (Bites, Dips, Additions, Salads, Flatbreads, Sandwiches; 28 priced rows) at medium confidence because it is roughly 2 years stale and the restaurant's own current site has nothing to check it against. Deliberately excluded the wine list: it is dated 2023 (3 years stale) and lists specific vintages (2021-2023) that a wine bar rotates constantly, so by-the-glass/bottle wine pricing from it would likely be wrong today even if the food prices have held up. Excluded the beer menu entirely -- link was broken even in the archive. No fresher source found (Yelp blocked outright by its own anti-bot page; a happy-hour listing site only gave dollar-off discounts, not base prices, so it could not corroborate or replace this).

name: Dannys Palm Bar and Grill
blocked: No website on file and no first-party site found (name is common enough that generic search does not surface one). No ordering platform: WebSearch confirms no DoorDash/UberEats/Grubhub delivery listing. Reachable menu sources are all tier-5 aggregators or barred farms: allmenus.com (Grubhub-owned, dated (c)2023, 13 priced burger items, Original Slam $8.75 / Super Slam $11.50 / Grand Slam $16.00), zmenu.com (Cloudflare-walled, even via r.jina.ai), restaurantguru.com (barred outright), sagemenu.com (no actual per-item menu on the page -- only customer review text mentioning 'burger $17' and 'Super slam cheeseburger($16)'), dannys-palm-bar-grill.weeblyte.com (barred farm domain), dannys-palm-bar-grill.res-menu.net (loaded blank -- no menu content in the HTML), hyperflyer.com (a delivery-price-comparison widget, not the restaurant's own prices, 403 on curl and its jina reading shows fee-inflated 'compare a $50 order' figures, not menu prices), Facebook (blocked/400 on curl). The one real per-item menu (allmenus) cannot be filed alone per the tier-5 rule, and the only thing that could corroborate it (sagemenu's review text) actually DISAGREES with it -- Super Slam quoted at $16 in a review vs $11.50 on allmenus, and a generic 'burger $17' vs the $8.75-$11 specialty range -- a gap too large to be a same-era markup and consistent instead with the allmenus listing being stale (dated 2023). Per the disagreement rule, that makes both numbers unreliable rather than confirming either. Blocking rather than filing a partial or a possibly-stale full list.
notes: No dishes captured. If revisited, try calling or a Chrome-equipped agent on Yelp's photo gallery (bot-walled to curl here) for a dated printed-menu photo, which would settle the price level.

name: Cafecito on Palm
blocked: No website on file in the batch. Found cafecitosd.com via search, but it no longer resolves in DNS at all (curl and r.jina.ai both fail to resolve it -- likely a lapsed/dead domain). A March 2025 Wayback snapshot of it shows the site was a Shopify-style storefront selling ONLY branded merchandise (mugs, tote bags, hats, long-sleeve tees) -- no food/drink menu page exists on the site at any point captured. No delivery platform found (no DoorDash/UberEats/Grubhub listing, no allmenus/menupages entry). joe.coffee has a location page for this cafe with reviews and hours but no priced items -- it's a client-rendered app with no menu data in the HTML and no embedded JSON to extract. sagemenu.com and Wheree.com (403) have no per-item pricing either, only review snippets that mention a couple of incidental dollar figures inside customer text ('burrito...for the price of $4', 'chamoy Tajin rim for $1 extra') which are not a menu and not safe to file as one. Address on file (1550 Palm Avenue) matches all sources found (1550 Palm Ave, San Diego, CA 92154).
notes: No dishes captured -- no reachable source publishes a priced menu for this cafe. Worth another look with a browser (Yelp's photo gallery is bot-walled to curl here and might hold a dated printed-menu photo) or by checking Instagram, which was not reachable from this environment.

name: The Pub at Lake Cuyamaca
notes: Own site, plain server-rendered HTML (SpotHopper-powered site, but the food menu page itself is static HTML with prices, not the tmt.spotapps.co widget). Header address '15027 CA-79, Julian' matches the batch address. Sections: Sharables, Salads, Soups, Handhelds, Burgers, Pub Favorites, Desserts, Breakfast (Sat/Sun 9-11am), Kids Menu, and a Dog Menu (priced treats for dogs, included as real priced menu rows though not human food). Checked the food page's own Beer list and the separate /julian-pub-at-lake-cuyamaca-drink-menu page (Wine: red/white/sparkling by name, Draft beer by name+ABV) -- neither carries a single dollar price anywhere; this is a beer/wine board that genuinely prints no per-item price (confirmed by reading both pages, not assumed), so it is correctly omitted rather than treated as a gap. The only priced line on the drinks page, 'Buy Kitchen a Round $5.00', is a gratuity/tip item, not a drink, and was dropped.
